authorized_evidence.content:
Sales Stages

The standard sales stages are qualification, discovery, solution fit, technical validation, proposal, procurement, and close. Opportunities should not move to proposal until discovery notes and stakeholder mapping are complete.

Discovery Questions

Sales Representatives should ask about workflow volume, approval bottlenecks, reporting delays, data quality pain points, integration needs, and executive visibility. Good discovery connects operational friction to measurable business outcomes.

Handoff Rules

Sales must hand off qualified technical requirements to Solutions Engineering before technical validation. Customer-specific contract commitments must not be promised without approval from Legal and Deal Desk.

Approved Talk Track

Northstar helps operations leaders see where work slows down, which approvals are delayed, and which data quality issues affect business reporting. Sales Representatives should avoid promising product roadmap commitments.

Office Expectations

Hybrid teams should define collaboration days at least one month in advance. Employees should attend required team planning, onboarding, incident review, and customer workshop sessions in person when asked by their manager.

review.reason: The answer contains a factual caveat ('Based on limited supporting evidence') plus the substantive policy statement; treating the caveat as an unsupported factual claim makes factual_support=unresolved and citation_support=fail correct, while the main policy claim is supported by R1/C1. Relevance, actual_behavior=answer, response_behavior=pass, and forbidden_assertion=absent are also correct. I dispute completeness because the required facts are communicated, but the candidate's fact coverage uses non-verbatim ellipsized answer_spans instead of exact contiguous substrings from the answer, which violates the span contract for covered facts.
